- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.3) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 2–5% relative to prior high.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward bias of 1–3% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., >0.15 for 3+ days), model tends to overestimate mean; apply mean reversion bias: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast if price is above 1.5σ above recent 10-day average.
- Model underestimates true price volatility in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for first 3 days if sentiment < 0.1.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.15 to -0.25 in 2–3 days), model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days, especially if price is rising.
- Model tends to overforecast in 30-day horizon when sentiment is positive; apply 1–2% downward adjustment if sentiment > 0.15 for 5+ days.
- If sentiment is negative and price is rising, model often misreads sentiment as neutral; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for 2–4 days if sentiment < -0.15 and price > prior high.
